title: Local Model Shadowing — Offline Failover + Latency Hedging (scratchpad)
content:
Problem framing:
We ship mobile/edge SDKs to customers who sometimes operate in degraded network conditions or behind strict firewalls. Applications need two related capabilities: graceful offline/poor-network behavior, and predictable low-latency responses even when the hosted path is available but slow. Today customers either: 1) rely on local heuristics and naive caching, or 2) build and maintain their own small local models and sync logic. That is heavy.

Proposal (working name): Local Model Shadowing (LMS)
High-level idea: provide an opt-in SDK feature that keeps a small quantized model and a compact KV cache on-device (or VPC-edge box) and "shadows" requests to the hosted/private Redwood runtime. The SDK uses the hosted inference by default but can return the local result when connectivity is poor or when latency-policy prefers local. While shadowing, the SDK still sends telemetry and lightweight request headers to the control plane so we can compare local vs hosted outputs and gradually improve local config.

Goals:
- Offline-first UX: provide useful fallback when host unreachable
- Latency hedging: return result from whichever (host/local) meets latency SLO for the route
- Quality observability: collect diffs between local and host to decide model updates/patches
- Minimal developer friction: single SDK flag and a few configuration knobs

Non-goals (for initial ship):
- Support for arbitrary customer models on-device (we'll start with curated quantized variants)
- Full parity with hosted model features (tools, function-calling, heavy multimodal ops)

Key components (sketch):
1) Local runtime bundle: tiny quantized model + lightweight tokenizer + inference harness (wasm/arm64). A couple of model variants (compact-chat, compact-completion) with strict token caps.
2) In-memory + persisted KV cache: stores prefix KV states and short recency cache of recent turns to reduce token usage locally.
3) SDK decision engine: runtime policy that chooses host vs local based on: network health probe, observed RTTs, explicit route SLOs, token budget, developer override.
4) Shadow telemetry pipeline: send anonymized deltas (hashes of input, quality score, latency, token counts) to Redwood control plane for offline analysis and model tuning.
5) Sync & update mechanism: periodic encrypted model delta check and incremental cache priming via small sync bundles when on good network.

Basic UX / config (SDK):
- enableLocalShadow: boolean
- preferredMode: [host-first, hybrid, local-first]
- latencyBudgetMs: integer
- maxLocalTokensPerTurn: integer
- telemetryConsent: [on, minimal, off]
Developer story: install SDK, call Redwood.generate with same options; optional localHints to prime cache; no extra endpoints required.

User stories (rough):
- As a mobile engineer, I want the app to return a short helpful answer within 300ms even if my network spikes, so users don’t see blank loading states.
- As an SRE for a customer, I want to toggle local-first in a feature flag to run a pilot among 10% of users.
- As a Redwood product manager, I want to collect mismatch stats so we can decide which compact model needs retraining.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SDK can run compact model on common arm64 phones with <250ms median local generation for 32-token responses
- SDK decision engine falls back to local after N consecutive host timeouts (configurable)
- Telemetry shows per-request whether returned by local/host and a simple similarity metric (bleu/embedding cosine), and appears in Console within 24h
- Encrypted model updates can be fetched over unreliable networks and applied atomically

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy / compliance: how much raw content can we send in telemetry? Need privacy-preserving diffs (hashes, coarse metrics). Consult security/legal.
- KMS for on-device keys: do we require customer-provided KMS for Private deployments? Edge cases for BYOK.
- Model maintenance: how to coordinate model drop-in replacements without breaking UX? Stale local models could diverge badly.
- Resource caps: battery and storage impacts on mobile; need clear minimum device specs and heuristics to auto-disable when constrained.
- Cost accounting: how to attribute token consumption when local falls back to host mid-request? Session-level accounting model needed.

Telemetry + Console needs:
- New Console panel: "Local Shadowing" with metrics: local_vs_host latency distribution, mismatch rate, examples (redacted), per-model performance, cohort toggles
- Rollout tooling: canary by user cohort, percentage, device class, region

Roadmap (tentative):
- Spike (2 weeks): PoC running a tiny quantized model in mobile simulator and a basic decision engine
- MVP (8 weeks): SDK flag, two compact models, telemetry pipeline, Console metrics, atomic model fetch
- Pilot (4 weeks): run with 2 customers on Redwood Private + hosted hybrid; gather mismatch data and perf stats
- v1 (quarter): add smarter KV cache priming, model auto-update policies, developer tooling for model selection

Implementation notes / quick tech bits:
- Use wasm for cross-platform runtime; native arm64 optimized path for Android/iOS later
- Store model blobs in app-private storage encrypted with device key; use periodic signed manifest from control plane to check versions
- Telemetry should use coarse similarity (embedding cosine) and hashed inputs to avoid raw PII leaks
- Consider offering an "offline bundle" option for Private customers: they can ship a vetted quantized model with their Private control plane image

Next steps (for me):
- Sync with Maya (SRE) and Ravi (Infra) to validate model fetch manifest & storage encryption assumptions
- Draft a short proposal for PM + Legal summarizing telemetry privacy tradeoffs
- Run a micro-benchmark on Pixel 5 and iPhone SE (simulator) with a 50M quantized variant to validate latency and memory

Notes to self: keep initial APIs tiny. Customers should be able to opt-in without rewriting prompts. Focus on observability — early mismatch signals are the most valuable product feedback.
